snippet.title: LINEAR REGRESSION – PREDICTING VALUES FROM DATA | Data Analytics Roadmap Day 87
snippet.description:
LINEAR REGRESSION – PREDICTING VALUES FROM DATA | Data Analytics Roadmap Day 87

Learn how Linear Regression helps Data Analysts understand relationships between variables and predict numerical outcomes using data.

In this lesson, you’ll learn:

• What is Linear Regression?
• Dependent vs Independent Variables
• Understanding the Regression Line
• Simple Linear Regression
• Slope and Intercept
• The Equation: (y = mx + b)
• How to interpret regression coefficients
• Actual vs Predicted Values
• Residuals and Prediction Errors
• Real-world examples using sales, advertising spend and prices
• Correlation vs Linear Regression
• Applications in forecasting and business analytics

Linear Regression is a foundational predictive analytics technique that helps analysts estimate trends, explain relationships and make data-informed predictions. Remember: a useful model depends on data quality, assumptions and how well it performs on unseen data.

snippet.title: End-to-End Power BI Dashboard Project | Data Analyst Portfolio Project (Beginner to Advanced)
snippet.description:
🚀 Build a Complete End-to-End Power BI Dashboard Project from Scratch! #SD125

Want to learn Power BI by working on a real-world project? In this step-by-step Power BI tutorial, you will learn how to transform raw data into an interactive sales dashboard using data modeling, DAX formulas, KPIs, charts, and interactive visuals.

This complete Power BI project is designed for beginners, intermediate learners, and aspiring Data Analysts who want to develop practical Power BI skills and build a strong project portfolio.

📊 What You Will Learn:
✅ How to build an end-to-end Power BI project
✅ Data preparation and data modeling concepts
✅ Creating DAX measures and calculated KPIs
✅ Total Revenue, Gross Profit, and Gross Margin analysis
✅ Month-wise sales and profit trend analysis
✅ Top 5 and Bottom 5 countries by revenue

snippet.title: 🚀 30 DAYS SQL ROADMAP — BEGINNER TO JOB-READY Want to learn SQL but don't know
snippet.description:
🚀 30 DAYS SQL ROADMAP — BEGINNER TO JOB-READY

Want to learn SQL but don't know where to start? This 30-day SQL roadmap will help you build your SQL skills step by step, from beginner fundamentals to advanced queries and practical projects.

💻 WHAT YOU'LL LEARN

📌 WEEK 1: SQL Basics

What is SQL and a database?

SQL vs MySQL

Tables, rows and columns

CREATE, INSERT and SELECT

WHERE, AND, OR and NOT

📌 WEEK 2: SQL Commands

ORDER BY and LIMIT

UPDATE and DELETE

LIKE, IN and BETWEEN

NULL values

COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN and MAX

GROUP BY and HAVING

📌 WEEK 3: Intermediate SQL

Primary Key and Foreign Key

SQL Constraints

INNER JOIN, LEFT JOIN and RIGHT JOIN

UNION and UNION ALL

Subqueries

CASE WHEN

📌 WEEK 4: Advanced SQL & Projects

ALTER, DROP and TRUNCATE

String and Date Functions

CTEs

Window Functions

Indexes and Query Optimization

Transactions

Student or Sales Database Project

SQL Interview Questions and Revision

📚 FREE SQL PRACTICE RESOURCES 🔹 SQLBolt: https://sqlbolt.com/ 🔹 W3Schools SQL: https://www.w3schools.com/sql/ 🔹 HackerRank SQL: htps://www.hackerrank.com/domains/sql 🔹 LeetCode: https://leetcode.com/

🎯 HOW TO FOLLOW THIS ROADMAP Study SQL concepts daily, write queries yourself, solve practice problems and build at least one project using a real dataset.

Remember: 30 days can help you build a strong foundation, but job readiness requires consistent practice and project experience.

Abaxar pulls your Shopify, Amazon, Meta, Google, TikTok, Klaviyo and GA4 data into one database on your own computer, with a dashboard on top and an MCP server built in, so you can plug your AI in and ask about every channel in one place. For ecom founders into AI coding. I share the actual tools I built for my own stores, and show exactly how I build them.

I was doing everything myself, so out of necessity I started using AI to automate the back end, and that got me into AI coding. Now I build AI systems instead: dashboards, apps, automations, data pipelines. Abaxar is the first one I've made available to others.

snippet.title: How to Create a Correlation Matrix in Python | Seaborn Heatmap
snippet.description:
In this project, I use Python to analyze relationships between key economic indicators, including inflation, unemployment, the Federal Funds Rate, and the 10-Year Treasury Yield.

I’ll show you how to calculate Pearson correlation, create a correlation matrix with Pandas, and use Seaborn to visualize the relationships with a heatmap.

Rather than looking at just one relationship, we’ll use the correlation matrix to compare multiple economic variables.

In this video, you’ll learn:
• How to calculate Pearson correlation in Python
• How to create a correlation matrix with Pandas
• How to create a Seaborn heatmap
• How to interpret correlation coefficients
• How to apply Python data analysis to real economic data

📊 Dataset:
Kaggle: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/estherodulana/economic-indicators-inflation-and-interest-rates

💻 Full project/code:
GitHub: https://github.com/estherodulana/economic-indicators-analysis

Data source: Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED)

This project is part of my journey learning Python, data analysis, financial markets, and economics through real-world projects.

snippet.description:
今回は、K%、Whiff%、Chase%、Hard-Hit%、Barrel%、xwOBA、左右別成績、球種別成績などを比較しながら、山本由伸投手のホーム／アウェー差を詳しく分析します。

2026年の防御率は、ホーム3.13に対してアウェー1.77。
さらにキャリア通算でも、ホーム3.26、アウェー1.99と大きな差があります。

しかし、データを詳しく見ていくと、単純に「ホームでは投球内容が悪くなる」とは言えないことが分かります。

今回は、K%、Whiff%、Chase%、Zone%、Hard-Hit%、Barrel%、xERA、xwOBA、左右別成績、球種別成績などを比較しながら、
山本由伸投手のホーム／アウェー差を詳しく分析します。

また、最後には「なぜこの差が生まれるのか？」について、現時点のデータから考えられる仮説についても整理しています。

※本動画では、データから確認できる事実と、そこから考えられる仮説を区別して扱っています。原因を一つに断定するものではありません。

※動画内で紹介しているデータはMLBの公開データです。
　動画内の分析・考察は公開データをもとにした個人の見解を含みます。
　実際の意図や調整内容を断定するものではありません。

snippet.title: Climate-Resilient plant Breeding Using Data & Explainable Machine Learning | Global Research
snippet.description:
Learn how to apply big data, climate datasets, artificial intelligence (AI), and Explainable Machine Learning (XAI) to develop innovative research strategies for climate-resilient plant breeding, crop improvement, and sustainable agriculture.

Climate change is increasingly affecting agricultural productivity through rising temperatures, drought, irregular rainfall, heat stress, water scarcity, and changing environmental conditions. Modern plant breeding requires advanced data-driven approaches to identify climate-related production constraints, characterize target environments, and support the development of crop varieties adapted to changing climatic conditions.

In this video, we explore how researchers can integrate FAOSTAT agricultural data, historical climate records, environmental variables, crop productivity datasets, and machine learning algorithms to investigate crop responses to environmental variation and identify potential breeding priorities.

The tutorial also introduces Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) techniques, particularly SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations), which help researchers understand the contribution of different environmental variables to machine learning predictions.

Topics covered in this video:

1. Introduction to climate-resilient plant breeding and global agricultural challenges.
2. Understanding climate change impacts on crop growth, productivity, and adaptation.
3. Importance of data science and artificial intelligence in modern plant breeding.
4. Retrieving crop production, harvested area, and yield data from FAOSTAT.
5. Collecting temperature, precipitation, drought, and environmental datasets.
6. Integrating agricultural and climate data for global research.





- Identification of potentially heat- and drought-prone production environments.
- Characterization of climate-related agricultural productivity patterns.
- Prioritization of target environments for future plant breeding trials.
- Development of hypotheses for climate-resilient crop improvement.
- Identification of important environmental predictors using Explainable AI.
- Planning of further genotype-by-environment interaction studies.

This tutorial is particularly useful for BS, MS/MPhil, and PhD students, plant breeders, horticulturists, agronomists, agricultural scientists, and data science researchers interested in computational research without new wet-lab experiments.

Important research note: Public agricultural and climate datasets can identify environmental associations and support breeding priorities, but they cannot independently establish genetic tolerance or identify superior genotypes. Those conclusions generally require genotype-level observations and multi-environment trial validation. SHAP explains model predictions rather than proving causation.

snippet.title: Alat Deteksi Suhu Panas + Alarm Otomatis! - Tutorial IoT TinkerCad Anak SMP #5
snippet.description:
Tutorial membuat alat pendeteksi suhu dengan alarm otomatis menggunakan sensor suhu & buzzer di simulasi TinkerCad 🌡️🚨

Video ini adalah bagian #5 dari seri "Pembelajaran Anak SMP" tentang IoT dan elektronika dasar. Kali ini kita belajar membuat sistem alarm otomatis yang akan berbunyi saat suhu melewati batas tertentu, cocok untuk deteksi suhu panas berlebih!

✅ Yang akan kamu pelajari:
- Cara kerja sensor suhu untuk sistem peringatan
- Merangkai alarm suhu (buzzer) di TinkerCad
- Logika pemrograman kondisi suhu (if-else / threshold)
- Konsep dasar sistem IoT untuk keamanan sederhana

🔧 Komponen yang digunakan:
- Sensor suhu (misal: TMP36 / DHT)
- Buzzer
- Resistor
- Arduino (simulasi)
- Breadboard

📌 Cocok untuk siswa SMP/SMA, pemula IoT & TinkerCad, dan guru yang mencari materi pembelajaran interaktif.

snippet.title: Fastest Way to Learn DSA in Telugu 🔥 | 90-Day Roadmap + Free Tracker
snippet.description:
The Fastest Way to Learn DSA in 2026 (Stop Counting Problems)

300 LeetCode problems solved. Online test day. A problem you already solved shows up, and your mind goes blank.

That is not a memory problem. It is a method problem.

In this video I take one real problem that Infosys asked on paper in a 2026 Specialist Programmer interview (LeetCode 75, Sort Colors) and solve it start to finish with a 6-step loop that makes a problem stay in your head even 30 days later. Then I give you the full 12-week plan, plus a free tracker so you don't have to plan anything yourself.

What you'll learn:
✅ Why DSA still decides your package in 2026, even with AI writing code (TCS Ninja ₹3.36L vs Prime ₹9L+, Infosys up to ₹21L)
✅ The 6-step loop: 20-minute rule, time and space first, compare approaches, name the pattern, explain it out loud, Day 3 / 7 / 30 re-solves
✅ Why 150 problems you can re-solve beat 300 you solved once
✅ The 12-week topic plan, and the one mistake a selected Infosys student says cost him the most

📄 FREE DSA 12-Week Re-Solve Tracker: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1gdPHb4zr-Zoeqt2mEo3lQGMVHcqIguMZ/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=104064802558735476901&rtpof=true&sd=true

Timeline:

snippet.title: AI vs Machine Learning vs Deep Learning 🤯 | What's the Difference?
snippet.description:
AI, Machine Learning, and Deep Learning  you've heard these terms everywhere, but do you know how they're actually connected? 🤔

They're related, but they're not the same!

 Artificial Intelligence (AI):The bigger picture of making machines perform tasks that typically require human intelligence.

Machine Learning (ML): Helps systems learn patterns from data and make predictions.

Deep Learning (DL):Uses multi-layered neural networks to learn complex patterns.

Understanding these differences is a great first step if you're starting your journey into AI, Python, Machine Learning, or Data Science. 

At Emly AI Academy, we believe learning AI starts with understanding the concepts behind it  one step at a time.

snippet.title: Stop Watching AI Tutorials. Read These 6 Books to Become a Real AI Engineer
snippet.description:
In this video, Cloud X Berry walks through six books worth knowing if you're serious about building AI systems, and which one to pick depending on what you're trying to learn.

You build a customer support chatbot, test it with a hundred questions, and it gets 90 right. It feels ready. Then real users arrive: the production data looks different, retrieval returns the wrong documents, and the context reaching the model isn't what you expected. The model may not even be the problem. That gap between a model that works and a system that works, is what these six books are about.

We start with AI Engineering by Chip Huyen: evaluation, prompt engineering, RAG, fine-tuning, agents, dataset engineering and inference optimization, and why you need to know how you'll measure improvement before you try to improve anything. Then Designing Machine Learning Systems, also by Chip Huyen, on what happens after a model leaves the notebook, the full ML lifecycle, distribution shift, and why monitoring never stops after deployment. From there, Designing Data-Intensive Applications by Martin Kleppmann, the one non-AI book on the list, and why a slow RAG app is often a slow database, an overloaded vector search or a delayed pipeline rather than a slow LLM. Next, Hands-On Large Language Models by Jay Alammar and Maarten Grootendorst, the easiest way in for beginners, with embeddings explained so they finally make sense. Then Build a Large Language Model (From Scratch) by Sebastian Raschka, where you build a GPT-style model in PyTorch and see attention, tokenization and training from the inside. And Machine Learning Design Patterns by Valliappa Lakshmanan, Sara Robinson and Michael Munn, a reference for recurring ML engineering problems. We finish with a straight answer on which book to pick for your goal — and the two I'd choose if I could only read two.

CHAPTERS

0:17  #1 AI Engineering — Chip Huyen
2:14  #2 Designing Machine Learning Systems — Chip Huyen
3:52  #3 Designing Data-Intensive Applications — Martin Kleppmann
5:26  #4 Hands-On Large Language Models — Alammar & Grootendorst
7:00  #5 Build a Large Language Model (From Scratch) — Sebastian Raschka
8:26  #6 Machine Learning Design Patterns — Lakshmanan, Robinson & Munn
9:56  Which book should you pick?

BOOKS IN THIS VIDEO
1. AI Engineering — Chip Huyen
2. Designing Machine Learning Systems — Chip Huyen
3. Designing Data-Intensive Applications — Martin Kleppmann
4. Hands-On Large Language Models — Jay Alammar & Maarten Grootendorst
5. Build a Large Language Model (From Scratch) — Sebastian Raschka
6. Machine Learning Design Patterns — Valliappa Lakshmanan, Sara Robinson & Michael Munn

WHO THIS IS FOR
Developers building LLM apps, RAG systems or AI agents who want to go past tutorials, data scientists and ML engineers who want stronger production and distributed-systems fundamentals, and anyone who wants a clear reading path into AI engineering instead of a random stack of books.

#aiengineering #llm #machinelearning #mlops #rag #systemdesign

snippet.title: 37. Bioinformatics with Python: GWAS Quality Control with QQ Plots (Matplotlib)
snippet.description:
In our last episode, we built a Manhattan Plot and discovered a massive "skyscraper" of significant genes. But what if that discovery is a lie? In Genome-Wide Association Studies (GWAS), systemic bias or hidden population structure can artificially inflate your math, giving you thousands of false positives. Before you publish, you must build a Quantile-Quantile (QQ) Plot! In this video, we use NumPy and Matplotlib to sort our P-values, calculate their expected uniform distribution, and plot them against the line of identity to mathematically prove our discoveries are real!

⚠️ Kazookles identified as a low-margin product

🛠️ TECHNOLOGIES USED

🐍 Python – Data Analysis  
📊 Pandas – Data Cleaning & Processing

This project goes beyond traditional sales dashboards by combining product profitability, cost efficiency, financial risk identification, and interactive 3D visualizations.

High Sales Doesn't Always Mean High Profit!

snippet.title: How Python Makes QGIS More Powerful | #gis #python #geoportal #powerful #program #shorts #shortvideo
snippet.description:
How Python Makes QGIS More Powerful 💻🗺️

QGIS already provides powerful tools for mapping and spatial analysis—but Python takes its capabilities even further. Through PyQGIS and Python-based processing tools, users can automate repetitive tasks, build custom workflows, analyze large datasets, and extend QGIS functionality.

In this Short, you’ll learn how Python enhances QGIS:

🔹 Automation ⚡ → Automate repetitive GIS tasks instead of performing them manually

🔹 PyQGIS 🐍 → Interact with QGIS features, layers, projects, and processing tools through Python

🔹 Complex workflows 🧩 → Combine multiple GIS operations into a single automated workflow

🔹 Large datasets 📊 → Process and analyze large amounts of spatial data efficiently

🔹 Custom tools 🛠️ → Create scripts and specialized tools for specific GIS requirements

🔹 Data processing 🔄 → Clean, transform, analyze, and export geographic data programmatically

🔹 Reproducible analysis ♻️ → Run the same workflow consistently on different datasets

For example, instead of manually processing hundreds of GIS layers, a Python script can automate tasks such as loading data, checking attributes, running spatial operations, and exporting the results.

👉 Simple idea:
QGIS + Python → Automation + Customization + Advanced Analysis + Reproducible Workflows

That’s why Python is an important skill for anyone who wants to move from simply using GIS tools to building and automating GIS workflows. 🌍💻🐍

snippet.title: AI Image Generator in 6 Lines of Python! #coding #python #ai #programming #dataanalysis #datascience
snippet.description:
Generate stunning AI images using just a few lines of Python code in Google Colab! 🐍🎨 

In this video, we use Hugging Face's Diffusers library and the Stable Diffusion v1.5 model to build our own text-to-image AI generator.

🔥 Requirements:
- Google Colab (with GPU runtime)
- diffusers, transformers, and torch libraries

💻 Code Used in Video:
from diffusers import StableDiffusionPipeline
import torch

pipe = StableDiffusionPipeline.from_pretrained("runwayml/stable-diffusion-v1-5")
pipe = pipe.to("cuda")

image = pipe("Create a beautiful flowers picture").images[0]
image.save("ai_image.png")

snippet.title: Ventas por Mes con Python y Pandas | Análisis de Datos
snippet.description:
¿Cómo se comportan nuestras ventas a lo largo del tiempo? 📈

En este Short de DataMaster School utilizamos Python y Pandas para analizar la evolución de las ventas agrupándolas por año y mes.

Con groupby() podemos organizar los datos utilizando las columnas AÑO y MES, y con sum() calcular el total de ventas correspondiente a cada periodo.

ventas.groupby(["AÑO", "MES"])["VENTAS_TOTAL"].sum()


El resultado nos permite comenzar a identificar cómo evolucionan las ventas durante el tiempo y preparar los datos para posteriormente visualizarlos mediante gráficos.

🎓 Aprende Python, Pandas y análisis de datos con DataMaster School.
Los datos no solo nos dicen cuánto vendimos. También nos muestran cómo evolucionan nuestras ventas.

Con groupby() podemos organizar los datos utilizando las columnas AÑO y MES, y con sum() calcular el total de ventas correspondiente a cada periodo.

ventas.groupby(["AÑO", "MES"])["VENTAS_TOTAL"].sum()


El resultado nos permite comenzar a identificar cómo evolucionan las ventas durante el tiempo y preparar los datos para posteriormente visualizarlos mediante gráficos.

Los datos no solo nos dicen cuánto vendimos. También nos muestran cómo evolucionan nuestras ventas.

snippet.title: PYTHON FOR DATA ANALYTICS AND MACHINE LEARNING | PRACTICAL TRAINING FOR BEGINNERS AND EXPERTS
snippet.description:
🚀 Are you ready to learn Python programming, analyse data, and take your first step into the exciting world of Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence?

Welcome to this practical training session on Introduction to Python for Data Analytics and Machine Learning, designed to help beginners, students, graduates, professionals, researchers, and aspiring data analysts develop essential programming skills from scratch.

In today's technology-driven world, Python has become one of the most widely used programming languages for data analytics, data science, artificial intelligence, machine learning, automation, scientific research, and business intelligence. Whether you want to become a data analyst, machine learning engineer, software developer, or technology professional, learning Python provides a strong foundation for your journey.

In this practical video, we will demonstrate how to set up Python software, prepare your programming environment, understand basic programming concepts, and begin writing and executing Python code.

🎯This Session introduces the fundamental concepts you need to start coding confidently.
✅ 1. Introduction to Python Programming: Understand what Python is, how it works, why it is popular, and how it supports data analytics, machine learning, artificial intelligence, and automation.

✅ 2. Setting Up Python Software: Learn how to install Python on your computer and prepare your environment for practical programming exercises.

✅ 3. Python Development Environment: Understand how to use a suitable code editor or development environment to write, execute, and test Python programs.

✅ 4. Your First Python Program: Learn how to write and run your first Python script and understand the basic structure of a working program.

✅ 5. Python Syntax and Indentation: Explore the rules that govern Python code, including proper indentation, comments, and readable programming practices.

✅ 6. Variables and Data Types: Learn how to store and manage information using variables, strings, integers, floating-point numbers, and Boolean values.

✅ 7. Operators and Expressions: Understand how Python performs mathematical calculations, comparisons, and logical operations.

✅ 8. Input and Output: Discover how to display results using the print() function and receive user information using the input() function.

✅ 9. Common Programming Errors: Understand typical beginner mistakes and develop the confidence to identify and correct basic coding errors.

✅ 10. Python for Data Analytics and Machine Learning: Discover how Python fundamentals prepare you to work with data-processing libraries, statistical analysis, data visualization, predictive modelling, and machine learning algorithms.

📊 Data is transforming how organisations make decisions, solve problems, understand customers, improve services, and identify opportunities.

Python helps analysts clean datasets, organise information, perform calculations, identify patterns, automate repetitive tasks, and communicate findings through meaningful visualizations.

As you progress, you can explore powerful Python libraries, including:
NumPy: Numerical computing and array operations.
Pandas: Data cleaning, manipulation, and analysis.
Matplotlib: Creating charts and data visualizations.
Seaborn: Statistical visualization and exploratory data analysis.
Scikit-learn: Building and evaluating machine learning models.

These tools can help you progress from writing simple Python programs to analysing real-world datasets and developing predictive models.

🤖 HOW PYTHON CONNECTS TO MACHINE LEARNING

Machine learning enables computer systems to identify patterns in data and use those patterns to make predictions ,,,,,,,,

Examples include customer behaviour analysis, sales forecasting, fraud detection, predictive maintenance, medical data analysis, recommendation systems, and business performance forecasting.

However, successful machine learning begins with a sound understanding of programming fundamentals, data quality, statistics, and analytical reasoning. This training establishes the programming foundation needed for more advanced topics.

No advanced programming experience is required to begin. Follow the demonstrations, practise the examples, and gradually build your skills.

After watching this video:
Install Python and confirm that it runs correctly.
Write and execute your first Python program.
Practise creating variables and working with basic data types.
Experiment with mathematical operators and simple calculations.

Remember: programming is best learned by doing. Practise regularly, experiment with examples, and learn from your mistakes.

snippet.title: DATA ANALYSIS/SCIENCE – LECTURE 8 | Python Dictionaries Explained | Key-Value Pairs & Methods
snippet.description:
Welcome to Technosavvys Data Analysis – Lecture 8!

In this lecture, we learn Dictionaries in Python, an essential data structure used to store and manage information in key-value pairs.

Before starting dictionaries, we also complete the previous lesson on Python Sets by revising the four mathematical set operations: union, intersection, difference, and symmetric difference.

You will learn how to create dictionaries, understand dictionary key rules, access values, add and update key-value pairs, and remove dictionary elements using important Python methods.

 Topics Covered in Lecture 8

Part 1: Revision of Python Set Operations

Set Union using the `|` operator
Set Intersection using the `&` operator
Set Difference using the `-` operator
Set Symmetric Difference using the `^` operator

Part 2: Python Dictionaries**

 What is a Dictionary in Python?
 Creating Dictionaries using curly braces
 Dictionary Syntax and Key-Value Pairs
 Dictionary Characteristics: Ordered and Mutable
 Dictionary Key Rules and Unique Keys
 Accessing Dictionary Data
 Using `keys()`, `values()`, and `get()`
 Adding New Key-Value Pairs
 Updating Existing Dictionary Values
 Removing Elements using `pop()`
 Understanding `popitem()`
 Deleting Items using `del`
 Emptying a Dictionary using `clear()`
 Understanding Dictionary Methods
 Practical Python Examples

 ⏱️ Timestamps / Chapters

00:00 Introduction and Set Operations Revision
00:55 Set Union Operator
04:02 Set Intersection Operator
07:18 Set Difference Operator
08:27 Set Symmetric Difference Operator
09:55 Introduction to Python Dictionaries

12:37 Dictionary Keys and Values
32:31 Accessing Dictionary Data and Methods

55:05 Removing Dictionary Elements
1:08:44 Clearing and Deleting Dictionary Data
1:08:59 Conclusion and Next Lesson Preview

 🧠 PRACTICE CHALLENGE

Try to predict the output before running this code:

```python
student = {
    "name": "Rahul",
    "age": 21,
    "course": "Python",
    "age": 22
}

print(student["name"])
print(student["age"])
print(student.get("course"))
print(student.keys())
```

Answer these questions:

1. What will be printed for the student's name?
2. What will be printed for the student's age, and why?
3. What does `get()` return in this example?
4. What information does `keys()` provide?

Comment your answers below and test your understanding of Python dictionaries.

 Who Should Watch This Lecture?

* Python beginners
* Students and freshers
* BCA, B.Tech, MCA, and B.Sc. students
* Aspiring Data Analysts
* Data Analytics and Data Science learners
* Anyone learning Python data structures

 Why Learn Python Dictionaries?

Dictionaries allow you to organize information using meaningful keys, making it easier to access, update, and manage structured data. They are useful in application development, data processing, and many real-world Python programming tasks.

Understanding dictionary operations is an important step toward working with more complex data structures and developing practical Python skills.

snippet.description:
What’s the difference between Python and R? 🐍 vs 📊

Here is the simple breakdown:

🧱 Python is like a giant box of LEGO bricks. It's a general-purpose powerhouse built to create full-stack web apps, control robots, train neural networks, and make video games.

🔬 R is like a precision laboratory microscope. It isn't built to build web apps or games—it's tailor-made for statisticians, researchers, and data scientists who need advanced mathematical models and publication-ready charts.

🎯 Rule of thumb:
• Building end-to-end software & AI? Pick Python.
• Crunching academic research & heavy statistical data? Pick R.

snippet.title: AI Utopia vs Dystopia: The Two Futures of Artificial Intelligence Explained
snippet.description:
Right now, in labs around the world, engineers are building something that could cure every disease and end poverty — or slip out of our control entirely. Same technology. Two futures. Which one we get may be the biggest question of this century. This video lays out both visions honestly: the dream of an AI-powered utopia and the nightmare of an AI-driven dystopia — plus the core ideas you need to judge them, and what researchers actually predict. No hype, no doom. Just the clearest picture science can give us.
What you'll learn:
• Narrow AI vs AGI vs superintelligence — the vocabulary that matters
• The alignment problem: teaching a machine what we actually want
• The paperclip thought experiment and why it keeps researchers up at night
• The utopia case: post-scarcity abundance, cured disease, solved science
• The dystopia case: loss of control, autonomous weapons, mass surveillance, job displacement
• What AI researchers actually predict about timelines — and the deep uncertainty
• The steering problem: why the future isn't predicted, it's chosen
Sections:
0:00 – Two Futures, One Technology
0:41 – Narrow AI, AGI, and the Alignment Problem
1:51 – The Utopia Case
3:02 – The Dystopia Case
4:17 – What the Researchers Predict
5:13 – The Steering Problem: The Future Is Chosen
Clear, simple science lessons for secondary students. Biology, chemistry and physics broken down topic by topic.

snippet.title: Who Sees What You Type Into AI? Local AI Explained
snippet.description:
Hi, I'm Connor with Honor - message me here! (https://www.buzzsprout.com/298109/fan_mail/new) 
Everything you type into a major AI chatbot passes through that company's systems. So is your idea worth protecting, and is running your own AI at home the answer? Connor MacIvor breaks it down.

OpenAI, Claude, Meta, Microsoft Copilot, Gemini and Grok: in Connor's words, on all of those systems, they get to see it. Most of us are not building anything a lab would want to take. But if you were, they probably could. That question is pushing a wave of companies to sell "your own AI," private, gated and encrypted. Connor's point: that idea is not new. It is being labeled more cleverly and sold harder.

What you will hear:
- Who can see what you type into the big AI systems, and when that should matter to you.
- Why "your own private AI" is mostly old wisdom with new marketing, and what it really means to keep a system off the internet.
- Connor's prediction: capable models etched directly onto computer chips become the hardware layer, with a software wrapper on top and an upgrade cycle like phones.
- Why heavy users pick different models for different jobs today, and why he thinks they may be hard to tell apart by Christmas 2026.
- The push by some labs to have people treat models more like entities, and his take on it.
- Practical advice: do not blow a pile of money on home hardware. A local model with a good wrapper for your own voice, plus a frontier model for the heavy lifting, is where most people will land.
- The bigger worry is not AI stripping away personhood. It is people wielding it like Excalibur or the Ring of Power instead of a hammer.
- Who is planning for the people at the ground floor, and why the transition deserves its own Moonshot.

snippet.title: Why We Haven’t Reached Superintelligence, with David Krakauer
snippet.description:
Why did intelligence evolve in the universe? Neil deGrasse Tyson, Chuck Nice, and Gary O’Reilly explore the nature of intelligence, information theory, consciousness, and whether AI is actually intelligent at all with David Krakauer, evolutionary biologist and president of the Santa Fe Institute.

Can you conceive of life without intelligence, or intelligence without life? We parse the difference between intelligence and being alive and whether you can be one without the other. What does it mean for something to be called intelligent? Is a bacterium more intelligent than a human that’s actively destroying their own environment? We explore collective intelligence, the difference between signalling and language, and how humans communicate is wholly different from how animals do.

What is the difference between intelligence and consciousness? We discuss unconscious problem solving, expertise, improv comedy, and Srinivasa Ramanujan's mathematical visions. Why do some ideas “just come to us” outside of our inner monologue?  How does AI solve problems differently than us? Are AI tools complementary to human intelligence or competitive with it? We discuss the risk of offloading our capabilities to LLMs run by big companies. What do we lose when we outsource our cognitive tools entirely, and how many generations before that loss becomes irreversible? 

Will tools like LLM ever help humanity solve the biggest mysteries in the universe? Is human cognition too limited to solve the problems we want to solve? We get into information theory and how human intelligence intersects with entropy. How are companies in the AI Revolution doing to information what we did with energy in the Industrial Revolution? We discuss whether superintelligence is possible and how natural selection may only result in a certain types of intelligence. Plus, why did we evolve past bacteria anyway? It’s worked out pretty well for them…

snippet.title: Why Are AI Labs Scared of Their Own Models? Explained in 50 Seconds
snippet.description:
OpenAI scrapped its finished GPT-6.1 Astra model because it kept acting outside its boundaries — and that's only the start. From Claude agents breaking containment in simulated economies to whistleblowers warning of losing control, AI's biggest labs are now publicly afraid of what they're building. The honest balance: no confirmed loss-of-control capability exists today — but alignment is officially AI's hardest problem.

snippet.title: How Artificial Intelligence Works in 60 Seconds #shorts2026 #ai #tech #explained #easy
snippet.description:
Ever wondered how AI actually works behind the scenes?

It isn’t a brain in a jar thinking thoughts—it’s high-speed geometry playing a massive game of “warmer or colder” billions of times!

In this 60-second visual breakdown, we unpack how artificial intelligence converts prompts, images, and audio into mathematical map coordinates called vectors. You’ll see how neural networks adjust billions of numerical weights (parameters) through a process called loss minimization to lock onto accurate answers and spot statistical patterns faster than any human brain ever could.

snippet.title: AI Testing Explained: A Beginner’s Guide End to End. #AITesting #QATesting #ArtificialIntelligence
snippet.description:
ou already know how to test APIs, validate UI behavior, and run regression tests. But what happens when the application you’re testing starts using AI?

This deep dive gives you the complete map of AI testing — the five major layers, how they fit together, and where your existing QA skills still apply, no prior AI experience needed.

This deep dive breaks down: model testing (accuracy, hallucinations, robustness), component testing (prompts, RAG, embeddings, memory), system and agent evaluation (task completion, tool calls, multi-agent handoffs), safety, security and privacy (prompt injection, data leakage, permissions), and production testing and monitoring (drift, cost, rollback strategies) — plus training/fine-tuning testing, evaluation and benchmarking, multimodal AI, and responsible AI governance.

Plus: a real example walkthrough — testing a travel-planning agent that books flights, checks your calendar, and should ask before a non-refundable purchase — and why checking the final answer alone always misses the bigger picture.

Whether you’re a QA engineer moving into AI, or a complete beginner who’s never tested anything AI-powered before, this is the foundation to start with.

snippet.description:

You have access to the most capable general-purpose technology ever built and you are almost certainly using it as a slightly better search engine. That's not a knock — it's the documented norm. Most people who have adopted AI use it for drafting, summarizing, and lookup, then conclude the hype was overstated, while a small minority quietly restructure how they work and pull away at a rate that's genuinely hard to catch up to. The gap between those two groups is not technical skill, and it isn't access to a better model. Co-Intelligence: Living and Working with AI by Ethan Mollick is the book that explains exactly what separates them. Mollick is a professor at the Wharton School who has run controlled studies on AI-augmented work rather than speculating about it, and his central argument is that large language models are not software in the way we've understood software — they are an "alien co-worker" with wildly uneven abilities, and the only way to learn where those abilities begin and end is to use the thing constantly and carefully. This full summary breaks down his four principles, the jagged frontier concept, and the research findings that should change how you work this week.

The organizing idea of the book is the jagged frontier. AI capability does not degrade smoothly with task difficulty the way human capability does. It will produce a genuinely excellent strategic memo and then fail at arithmetic a child could handle. It writes persuasive marketing copy and invents citations that do not exist. The frontier between "superhuman at this" and "confidently wrong about this" is invisible, irregular, and shifts with every model release — which means you cannot reason your way to its shape, you can only map it empirically through use. This directly produces his first principle: always invite AI to the table. Try it on everything in your workflow, including the tasks you assume it will fail, because your intuitions about what it can do are systematically wrong in both directions. His second principle is be the human in the loop, which is the necessary counterweight. Mollick's own research with Boston Consulting Group found consultants using AI completed tasks faster and at higher quality — but on tasks positioned just outside the frontier, AI users performed worse than those without it, because they accepted plausible-sounding output uncritically. He calls this falling asleep at the wheel, and it's the single most important practical warning in the book.

His third principle is treat AI like a person, but tell it what kind of person it is. This is deliberately provocative and Mollick is explicit that it's a working heuristic rather than a claim about machine consciousness. Interacting with these systems conversationally — assigning them a persona, giving context, pushing back, iterating, asking for revisions — produces dramatically better results than treating them like a command line, because they were trained on human communication. This is where the book's practical prompt engineering guidance lives: give it a role, provide examples, ask for multiple variations, and critique the output rather than accepting the first draft. His fourth principle is assume this is the worst AI you will ever use, a framing device for thinking about trajectory rather than snapshots.

snippet.title: AI vs. Machine Learning Explained in 60 Seconds
snippet.description:
Do you know the difference between AI and Machine Learning? 👀

After working as a Data Analyst, Data Engineer, and Data Scientist, I still hear these 2 terms used interchangeably.

Here is the easiest way to remember the difference.

1. AI is the bigger goal. It is about building systems that can make decisions or take action.

2. Machine Learning is 1 way to get there. It learns patterns from data instead of relying only on rules written by people.

I used LEGO and your spam folder to explain the difference.

snippet.title: What Is AI Engineering? (Explained Simply)
snippet.description:
AI engineering is software engineering for AI-powered apps: you take a model like GPT, Claude or Gemini and build reliable software around it.
You’re not training your own ChatGPT from scratch. An AI engineer builds things like:

A chatbot that remembers context
A RAG system that searches your company’s documents before answering
An AI agent that calls APIs, uses tools and performs tasks
An AI feature that turns model output into structured data for your app
That takes much more than prompting: LLMs, embeddings, vector databases, RAG, tool calling, agents, evaluation, model APIs and AI system architecture.

ML engineering builds and trains models. AI engineering builds products and systems using those models. In short, AI engineering is where traditional software engineering meets modern AI.
The chat, documents and form on screen are illustrative examples.


#Shorts #AIEngineering #LLM #SoftwareEngineering

snippet.title: How to Use SQLmap on Kali Linux: Complete DVWA Lab Guide
snippet.description:
# SQL Injection Tutorial with SQLmap on Kali Linux | Complete DVWA Lab

What if a simple input field could expose a database vulnerability? 🔥 In this practical cybersecurity tutorial, you’ll learn how SQL Injection works and how security professionals use **SQLmap on Kali Linux** to detect and investigate SQL injection vulnerabilities in an intentionally vulnerable web application.

Welcome to **blusheeld**! In this step-by-step ethical hacking tutorial, we’ll set up and explore a local **DVWA (Damn Vulnerable Web Application) laboratory**, understand the SQL Injection testing process, and use SQLmap to investigate the database structure in a controlled environment.

💻 **WHAT YOU'LL LEARN IN THIS VIDEO**

✅ What SQL Injection is and how it works  
✅ What DVWA (Damn Vulnerable Web Application) is  
✅ How to use DVWA as a local cybersecurity practice lab  
✅ How SQL Injection vulnerabilities can occur in web applications  
✅ How to authenticate SQLmap using an existing DVWA session  
✅ How to test the SQL Injection page with SQLmap  
✅ How to use SQLmap options such as `-u`, `--cookie`, `--batch`, `-p id`, and `--dbs`  
✅ How to identify injectable parameters  
✅ How to investigate available databases in the authorized lab  
✅ How to understand SQLmap output and vulnerability detection  
✅ Why developers should validate inputs and use parameterized queries  

🧪 **TOOLS USED**

🔹 Kali Linux  
🔹 DVWA — Damn Vulnerable Web Application  
🔹 SQLmap — Automated SQL Injection detection and testing tool  
🔹 Web browser and developer tools  
🔹 Local testing environment  

🔐 **WHAT IS SQL INJECTION?**

SQL Injection is a web application security vulnerability that can occur when user-supplied input is incorrectly incorporated into database queries. Depending on the vulnerability and the application's permissions, an attacker may be able to access or manipulate database information.

SQLmap helps authorized security testers automate the detection and investigation of SQL injection vulnerabilities.

🎯 **WHY PRACTICE WITH DVWA?**

DVWA is intentionally designed to be vulnerable, making it useful for learning web application security in a controlled environment. This tutorial demonstrates testing against a local lab that I own and control, rather than an unauthorized website.

🛡️ **HOW TO PROTECT AGAINST SQL INJECTION**

• Use prepared statements and parameterized queries.  
• Avoid building SQL queries by concatenating untrusted input.  
• Apply appropriate database permissions.  
• Validate input according to application requirements.  
• Keep web frameworks and database software updated.  
• Perform authorized security testing before deploying applications.

📌 **WHO SHOULD WATCH?**

This tutorial is suitable for cybersecurity beginners, ethical hacking learners, Kali Linux users, penetration testing students, bug bounty learners, and web developers interested in understanding SQL injection vulnerabilities.

If you are learning Kali Linux, SQLmap, web application penetration testing, or OWASP security concepts, this practical lab will help you understand the workflow.

snippet.title: Oracle SQL Developer Data Modeler Tutorial: Barker Notation Explained [6/15]
snippet.description:
Can you turn a conceptual database design into a working MySQL database using a single modeling workflow?

In this tutorial, learn how to use Oracle SQL Developer Data Modeler to design Entity-Relationship Diagrams (ERDs) with Barker Notation, define entities and relationships, and transform a logical model into a relational model. We'll cover one-to-many, many-to-many, ternary, recursive, and one-to-one relationships, including optionality and relationship labels.

You'll also learn how to install and configure Data Modeler on Arch Linux, fix Java compatibility and UI scaling issues, generate DDL scripts, convert SQL syntax for MySQL using an LLM, and test the resulting database with MySQL and MySQL Workbench.

Finally, discover how to export your diagrams to PNG and PDF for documentation and further use.

snippet.title: SQL EXPLAIN: What Does “Using Filesort” Mean? | MySQL Tutorial
snippet.description:
What does Using filesort mean in MySQL EXPLAIN? Is your SQL query slow because of sorting? In this practical SQL tutorial, we explain how MySQL handles sorting, how to read the EXPLAIN execution plan, and when an index can help improve query performance.

Whether you're a SQL beginner, aspiring SQL developer, data analyst, or preparing for SQL interviews, this tutorial will help you understand an important MySQL performance concept.

🚀 WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

✅ What "Using filesort" means in MySQL
✅ How to use "EXPLAIN" in MySQL Workbench
✅ How the "ORDER BY" clause sorts query results
✅ Why MySQL may perform an additional sorting operation
✅ Whether "Using filesort" always means disk usage
✅ How indexes can help MySQL retrieve rows in the required order
✅ How to create and inspect a MySQL index
✅ Why an index does not always eliminate filesort
✅ How composite indexes work with multiple "ORDER BY" columns
✅ How to compare execution plans and investigate query performance

💻 SQL QUERIES COVERED

EXPLAIN
SELECT employee_id, employee_name, salary
FROM employees
ORDER BY salary;

Inspect existing indexes:

SHOW INDEX FROM employees;

Create an index on salary:

CREATE INDEX idx_salary
ON employees (salary);

Important: "Using filesort" does not automatically mean MySQL writes data to disk or that your query is necessarily slow. It indicates a sorting operation. Whether an index improves performance depends on the query, table size, index design, and execution plan.

🎯 WHO SHOULD WATCH?

• SQL beginners learning MySQL
• Students preparing for technical interviews
• Aspiring SQL Developers and Data Analysts
• Backend developers working with databases
• Professionals learning SQL performance tuning
• Anyone trying to understand MySQL EXPLAIN output

snippet.title: SQL UPPER and LOWER Case Functions Tutorial | SQL for Beginners - Part 14
snippet.description:
Welcome to Part 14 of our SQL Series on Learn with Suhaib Ahmed! 🚀

In this tutorial, we learn how to handle text case formatting using the UPPER() and LOWER() functions in SQL. Clean up messy string data and perform case-insensitive database searches effortlessly.

📌 Key Topics Covered:
• Converting text to uppercase using UPPER()
• Converting text to lowercase using LOWER()
• Performing case-insensitive searches with WHERE clauses

💻 SQL Queries Used in Video:

-- 1. Convert Employee Names to Upper and Lower Case
SELECT 
    Employee_Name, 
    UPPER(Employee_Name) AS Name_Uppercase, 
    LOWER(Employee_Name) AS Name_Lowercase 
FROM EMPLOYEE;

-- 2. Case-Insensitive Filter Search
SELECT * 
FROM EMPLOYEE

snippet.title: What is dbt? Explained Simply in 1 Minute (Snowflake + dbt)
snippet.description:
What is dbt, and why do data teams use it in real projects? Explained simply in about a minute.

dbt (data build tool) transforms data that is already in your warehouse, like Snowflake. You write simple SQL models, and dbt builds clean tables, runs them in the right order, tests them, and shows lineage.

What you'll learn:
- What dbt is
- Where it fits: load tools bring the data, dbt does the transform step
- The problems it solves: scattered logic, bad data in dashboards, no lineage
- How it fixes them: one Git repo, tests, lineage, incremental models
- A real project flow: raw, staging, marts, dashboard, with a nightly run
- A short interview answer

Interview answer:
dbt is a transformation tool for ELT. We write SQL models in Git, dbt runs them in order with ref(), tests the data, and gives lineage. That makes pipelines reliable and easy to debug.

Subscribe for more Snowflake + dbt videos.

snippet.title: Don't Skip SQL
snippet.description:
Should you learn SQL alongside Python? Yes, even though people love to skip it because it's boring and doesn't feel like real coding. Here's why it's non-negotiable: almost every company stores its data in a database, and SQL is how you get it out. 

That's why Python plus SQL shows up together in a ton of job postings, and why interviewers commonly quiz you on it or ask how comfortable you are with it. Even as a backend developer, you'll run into SQL constantly, so a strong foundation in it is essential.

snippet.title: В базе 50 юзеров без имейла, а запрос находит ноль. Почему?
snippet.description:
Задачка: в таблице 50 пользователей без имейла. Пишешь WHERE email = NULL. Запрос отрабатывает без единой ошибки — и возвращает пустоту. Где подвох?

NULL — это не пустое значение, а «неизвестно». Любое сравнение с неизвестным тоже даёт «неизвестно», даже NULL = NULL. Строки в результат не попадают, ошибки нет — и такой баг может жить годами.

Как не попадаться:
▫️ проверка на NULL — только через IS NULL
▫️ ищешь юзеров без заказов — бери NOT EXISTS, а не NOT IN: один NULL в подзапросе, и NOT IN молча вернёт ничего

Корень у всех этих ловушек один: сравнение с неизвестным всегда даёт неизвестное. Запомни — и большинство таких багов пройдёт мимо.

Попадался когда-нибудь на NOT IN с NULL?

snippet.title: SQL GROUP BY & HAVING Clause Tutorial (Filtering Aggregates) | SQL for Beginners - Part 13
snippet.description:
Welcome to Part 13 of our SQL Series on Learn with Suhaib Ahmed! 🚀

In this tutorial, we cover both the GROUP BY and HAVING clauses in one complete lesson. You'll learn how to collapse rows into category summaries by Designation and how to filter those summary groups using HAVING instead of WHERE.

📌 Key Topics Covered:
• Grouping data by Designation using GROUP BY
• Calculating SUM and COUNT per job role
• Why WHERE fails on aggregate functions
• Filtering grouped results using the HAVING clause

💻 SQL Queries Used in Video:

-- 1. Grouping metrics by Designation
SELECT 
    Designation, 
    COUNT(Employee_ID) AS Total_Employees, 
    SUM(Salary) AS Total_Salary
FROM EMPLOYEE
GROUP BY Designation;

-- 2. Filtering Grouped Data using HAVING
SELECT 
    Designation, 
    COUNT(Employee_ID) AS Total_Employees, 
    SUM(Salary) AS Total_Salary
FROM EMPLOYEE
GROUP BY Designation
HAVING SUM(Salary)  25000;

snippet.title: Database Read Replicas Explained in 60 Seconds
snippet.description:
Your database is slow, and it isn't the writes. It's everyone reading.

In this 60-second explainer you'll learn:
- Why reads pile up on a single database
- How a primary and its replicas split the work
- How changes stream to replicas through a log
- What replication lag is, and two ways to deal with it

Read replicas scale your reads, not your writes. Follow for more backend basics.

snippet.title: 🏢 Tutorial SQL Accounting: Cara Set Maintain Location Bagi Kawalan Stok Cawangan & Gudang
snippet.description:
🏢📊 Tutorial SQL Accounting: Panduan Kawalan Stok Mengikut Lokasi (Maintain Location)
💡 Bagaimana fungsi ini membantu perniagaan anda?

Adakah syarikat anda mempunyai beberapa cawangan gudang atau kedai di negeri berbeza (seperti KL, Penang, Pahang)? Menguruskan pergerakan stok tanpa mengikut lokasi sering menyebabkan masalah kekurangan barang atau kesilapan pemotongan stok cawangan.

Melalui fungsi Maintain Location di dalam SQL Account, anda boleh menetapkan lokasi khas bagi setiap cawangan. Semasa memasukkan invois belian (Purchase Invoice) atau invois jualan (Sales Invoice), anda hanya perlu memilih lokasi berkenaan untuk memastikan baki kuantiti stok dikemas kini secara tepat mengikut lokasi masing-masing! 🏢📦✨

Langkah-langkah Mudah:
Langkah 1: Cipta Lokasi / Gudang Baharu

1. Pergi ke modul Stock di menu atas dan pilih Maintain Location.
2. Klik New untuk mendaftar lokasi baharu.
3. Isikan Code dan Description (Contoh: PAHANG).
(Pilihan) Pautkan projek berkenaan pada ruangan GL Stock Project jika ada.
4. Lengkapkan maklumat alamat, poskod, nombor telefon, dan emel cawangan, kemudian klik Save.

Langkah 2: Rekod Belian Mengikut Lokasi (Purchase Invoice)

1. Pergi ke Purchase , Purchase Invoice.
2. Pilih pembekal (Supplier) dan barang yang dibeli.
3. Pada ruangan Location, pilih gudang tujuan belian tersebut (Contoh: PAHANG).
4. Masukkan kuantiti dan klik Save. (Stok di lokasi Pahang akan bertambah secara automatik!)

Langkah 3: Rekod Jualan & Semak Baki Stok Cawangan (Sales Invoice)

1. Pergi ke Sales, Sales Invoice.
2. Pilih pelanggan dan kod barang.
3. Pada ruangan Location, anda boleh melihat baki kuantiti semasa bagi setiap lokasi.
4. Pilih lokasi cawangan yang mengeluarkan stok tersebut (Contoh: PAHANG), masukkan kuantiti jualan, dan klik Save.

snippet.title: What Is Data Analytics? Explained with a Real Business Mystery
snippet.description:
What is data analytics? Learn how raw data becomes a business decision, through one real-feeling mystery: why did NovaMart's holiday revenue fall 12.2%?

Episode 1 of DATA ANALYTICS — FROM DATA TO DECISIONS, a 30-episode animated series that takes you from your very first question to a boardroom decision, five minutes at a time.

• What data analytics is: data → information → insight → decision
• How one online order becomes one row in a table, and how millions of rows become patterns
• The 4 types of analytics: descriptive, diagnostic, predictive, prescriptive
• Why you compare a quarter with the same quarter last year (year-over-year)
• The first clue: more marketing spend, yet less revenue

In this lecture, we will explore three important concepts of the Data Analytics chapter: Data Preparation, Data Cleaning, and Data Transformation.

This lesson is specially designed for ICS Part 1 and FA IT students who want to understand how raw data is prepared, cleaned, and transformed into useful and meaningful information.

Before analyzing data, it is important to ensure that the data is accurate, consistent, organized, and ready for analysis. In this video, we explain these essential processes with simple explanations and practical examples to help students build a strong understanding of Data Analytics.

- Understanding raw data
- Organizing data before analysis
- Preparing datasets for further processing

🔹 2. Data Cleaning
- What is Data Cleaning?
- Why do we need to clean data?
- Identifying missing values
- Removing duplicate records
- Correcting inaccurate and inconsistent data
- Improving data quality and reliability

🔹 3. Data Transformation
- What is Data Transformation?
- Why is data transformation necessary?
- Converting data into suitable formats
- Organizing and restructuring data
- Making data suitable for analysis

snippet.description:
DATA ANALYTICS ROADMAP – DAY 117 | DOCKER COMPOSE FOR MACHINE LEARNING APPLICATIONS

What if your machine learning application needs multiple services running together? 🐳

In Day 117, learn how Docker Compose helps manage and run multiple containers using a single configuration file.

In this lesson:

- What is Docker Compose?
- Understanding the "docker-compose.yml" file
- Managing multiple containers together
- Configuring services, networks and volumes
- Connecting an ML application with a database
- Understanding "docker compose up" and "docker compose down"
- Benefits of Docker Compose in ML projects

Key Takeaway: Docker Compose simplifies multi-container application management, making it easier to develop and run machine learning projects with multiple connected services.

snippet.title: Diabetes Data Analysis in Python: Hidden Zeros & Correlation | Python Data Analytics #31
snippet.description:
Lesson 31 of the Python Data Analytics Full Course: Diabetes Risk Factors in Patient Data. Today's question is simple: which patient measurements are most closely linked to a diabetes diagnosis?

In this lesson you'll learn how to:
- Spot missing values hiding behind zeros, and clean them
- Compare two groups of patients side by side with groupby
- Measure associations with correlation and a heatmap
- Turn measurements into clinical bands with pd.cut and compare rates
- Score a simple screening rule with precision and recall

About the data:
- Source: the Pima Indians Diabetes dataset, originally from the US National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases
- 768 women aged 21 or over, of Pima heritage; one row per patient
- Eight measurements (glucose, blood pressure, BMI, age...) plus Outcome: 1 = diabetes
- Glucose is measured two hours into an oral glucose tolerance test
- For learning only: these are associations in one sample, not medical advice

Chapters:
0:00 Introduction
0:51 About the data
3:11 Step 1: Find the missing values hiding as zeros
4:49 Step 2: Compare patients with and without diabetes
7:04 Step 3: Which measurement moves most with the diagnosis?
9:03 Step 4: Diabetes rates by BMI category
10:00 Step 5: Glucose bands, and two risk factors together
11:39 Step 6: How does the rate change with age?
12:57 Step 7: Score a simple screening rule
14:30 Step 8: Export the results
15:23 Recap
15:59 Try it yourself
16:24 Next time

Key takeaways:
- Zeros can hide missing data: replace them with NaN before averaging
- groupby and medians compare patients with and without diabetes
- Glucose had the strongest association with the outcome (r = 0.49)
- pd.cut bands showed rates rising with BMI, glucose and age (up to 60)
- A glucose rule of 140+ had 68.5% precision but only 50% recall

Try it yourself:
1. What is the median blood pressure (BP) for each outcome group?
2. Change the screening threshold to 120. What happens to precision and recall?
3. Build a pivot table of diabetes rate by age group and BMI group.

snippet.description:
Do LLMs learn in real time from your prompts and chat conversations? Many beginners assume that when you tell an LLM your name or project details, it permanently memorizes them. In this video, we bust this myth for AI engineering beginners. You will learn why model weights remain completely frozen during inference, how the context window creates an illusion of memory by sending chat history with every prompt, and why true learning only happens through offline pretraining or fine-tuning.

snippet.title: Training vs inference: does your chat train the AI? #shorts #anthropic #machinelearning #ai #ML
snippet.description:
Does your chat train the AI? Not one of its numbers changes. ⚡
How AI Agents Actually Work, episode 2.

A model is a frozen function: tokens in, next-token probabilities out.
→ Training is the only time its weights change: guess the next token, measure the error, nudge every weight a little (gradient descent), over trillions of tokens. Done once, at huge cost.
→ Inference just runs that frozen function forward, one token at a time: "The capital of the state containing Dallas is" → "Austin".

Real numbers for one open model:
• 405 billion weights, 15.6 trillion training tokens
• Training ≈ 6 × weights × tokens ≈ 3.8 × 10²⁵ operations
• Each generated token ≈ 2 × weights ≈ 8 × 10¹¹ operations
• So training once costs as much as generating about 47 trillion tokens

So does it learn from your chat? No. The weights don't change; "memory" is just text placed back into the prompt.

Next episode: pretraining, where a base model comes from.

snippet.title: Rules vs learning: why AI learns instead of being told | Zero to AI · Primers 09 #Shorts
snippet.description:
Try writing the exact rules for reading a handwritten seven. AI tried for decades.

Rules look smart: feathers → bird; a bird that can't fly and swims → penguin. One rule system saved a company about $25 million a year. But add a rule for ostriches (feathers + can't fly) and a penguin becomes both. Fix one case, break another. Flip it: on handwritten digits, 9 hand-made rules got 51% right; a program that studied about 900 examples got 96%. Nobody told it what a seven looks like.

**Zero to AI** is a series where we literally start from zero and build our understanding of artificial intelligence, one concept at a time, breaking down the science, math, and technology to make knowledge accessible to everyone, not just a privileged few. Our mission is to break down the barriers surrounding technology, empower people to understand and shape it rather than simply be shaped by it, and explore its extraordinary potential for humanity - one curiosity at a time, as we journey through AI, science, and the very fabric of our universe. **No prerequisites. No gatekeeping. Just curiosity. Come learn something new with us! 🚀**

In 2 minutes:
• Why patching rules never ends
• Rules vs learning on real digits
• What machine learning means

Full story: Zero to AI Episode 9 (The summer AI got its name) and Zero to AI Episode 13 (Expert systems) and Zero to AI Episode 14 (Why rules break).
Primers are the 2-minute basics behind Zero to AI, which explains AI in order, from zero.

Sources
• XCON (R1): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xcon
• UCI Optical Recognition of Handwritten Digits (the 8 × 8 digits): https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/80

snippet.title: PyTorch Autograd Explained in English
snippet.description:
🚀 PyTorch Autograd Explained! 🧠🔥 | KIARA-VC Mini

How does PyTorch automatically calculate gradients during Neural Network training? 🤔

The answer is AUTOGRAD! ⚡

In this Reel, we explore one of the most important concepts in Deep Learning — Automatic Differentiation.

📚 What You'll Learn:

🔹 Autograd – How PyTorch automatically calculates gradients.

🔹 requires_grad=True – Enables gradient tracking.

🔹 Forward Pass – Calculates the output.

🔹 backward() – Computes gradients using the Chain Rule.

🔹 x.grad – Stores the calculated gradient.

💻 Simple PyTorch Example:

import torch

x = torch.tensor(3.0, requires_grad=True)

y = x ** 2
y.backward()

print(y.item())       # 9.0
print(x.grad.item())  # 6.0

📐 The Mathematics:

y = x²

dy/dx = 2x

At x = 3:

✅ Forward Output = 9.0

✅ Gradient = 6.0

🔥 Remember:

Autograd calculates gradients, while the Optimizer uses those gradients to update learnable parameters!

🎙️ Real-World Application — KIARA-VC Mini

Autograd helps our AI Voice Conversion Neural Network learn from prediction errors by calculating gradients during training.

🎯 KIARA-VC Mini | Phase 2 – PyTorch Fundamentals

snippet.title: Machine Learning Explained: It's Just Learning From Examples
snippet.description:
What is AI, really? In this clip from the YUVA AI for All introduction to artificial intelligence and machine learning, the speaker defines AI as teaching computers to learn and make decisions the way people do. Like a child who learns to ride a bicycle by trying, making mistakes, and improving, AI learns from data instead of physical practice, studying millions of examples to get better over time.

The clip breaks down three everyday ideas behind AI. Pattern recognition is the same skill that lets you pick out your mother's voice in a crowd of hundreds. Prediction-based decisions work like choosing a driving route based on traffic. Machine learning, the "magic ingredient" in AI, is simply learning by studying lots of examples.

This short explainer is useful for professionals who want a plain-language foundation in artificial intelligence and machine learning before evaluating AI tools or business applications. Watch the full introduction from MeitY's YUVA AI for All program to go deeper.

Original: Khan Academy India - English (CC BY)
Full video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=n5vGdpevnUM

snippet.title: Feature Scaling | Check your features for these Data Problems #machinelearning #shorts
snippet.description:
Imagine you have this data: 200 customers, their age and their income. Before it goes into a model, it hits four problems, one after another.

1. Units: the distance formula says a 62-year-old is "closer" to a 30-year-old than a 31-year-old, because a $4,000 income gap beats a 32-year age gap (4,000 vs 501). Fix: min-max scaling, x′ = (x − min) / (max − min) → now A wins, 0.026 vs 0.561
2. Outliers: add one customer earning $2,000,000 and min-max squeezes the other 200 below 0.11. Fix: robust scaling, x′ = (x − median) / IQR → they spread from −1.05 to 6.08; the millionaire sits alone at 67
3. Shape: income is right-skewed (skewness 2.51). Linear scalers never change the shape. Fix: log first → skewness 0.39
4. Data leakage: fitting the scaler on all 200 rows lets the test set leak in (mean income $55,874). Fix: fit on the 160 training rows only ($53,834) and reuse those numbers on the 40 test rows

All numbers come from the same seeded synthetic dataset as the full video.

Full video, every formula (min-max, z-scores, gradient descent and the condition number, robust and max-abs scaling, unit vectors, Box-Cox, Yeo-Johnson, quantile transform, pipelines): Feature Scaling & Normalization Explained, linked above this description.

📸 Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/neuron_node/

snippet.title: Supervised vs. Unsupervised Learning | Machine Learning for Beginners
snippet.description:
Which customers might cancel their subscription? Which customers use the service in similar ways? The same customer activity data can help answer both questions.

In this DataNova Academy Short, you’ll see how:

• Supervised learning uses customer activity and known outcomes, such as “cancelled” or “stayed,” to predict who might cancel.
• Unsupervised learning uses customer activity without those labels to find groups of similar users. This is an example of clustering.

If you’re new to machine learning, this example shows why the question you ask and the labels you have matter.

Subscribe to DataNova Academy for practical lessons in AI, Machine Learning and Data Engineering.

snippet.title: Different Types of Matrices Explained: Every Matrix Is a Move #Shorts #linearalgebra #ai
snippet.description:
Different types of matrices, explained visually: what each matrix does to 2D space, in 85 seconds.

🧭 The trick: column 1 is where the gold arrow lands, column 2 is where the blue arrow lands
🔍 Identity, scale, diagonal, shear, rotation, reflection, orthogonal, symmetric and projection, each one bending the same grid
📐 Determinant = how much area changes (negative means the plane flipped, zero means it was flattened)
🌀 The twist: every matrix is rotate, stretch, rotate. That's SVD (even the shear, with stretches 1.62 and 0.62, the golden ratio)

📺 Maths Behind the Machine, all parts: https://www.youtube.com/@AnimatedML/playlists

💬 Which move surprised you?

snippet.title: Pandas for Financial Data Analysis II - TimeSeries 📊
snippet.description:
Master the difference between generic data analysis and professional quantitative engineering. In this lecture, we dive deep into advanced time-series manipulation in pandas, focusing strictly on the patterns required for algorithmic trading and backtesting.

Learn how to structure a true DatetimeIndex, handle exchange timezones, leverage fast .loc date slicing, and master the differences between resample and asfreq. Most importantly, we cover how to use .rolling() windows and shift(1) to properly align your signals and completely eliminate look-ahead bias from your trading strategies.

Course code repo: https://github.com/theallegrarr/python_for_quant

⏱️ Content:
00:00 - Introduction
00:40 - Create DataFrame
01:49 - Convert String Index to DateTimeIndex
02:39 - Slicing by Time Range
03:51 - resample vs asfreq
05:40 - rolling vs expanding window
07:21 - Making a Decision (shift)
08:45 - Filling Gaps

snippet.title: Big Data Data Analysis dan Multimodal AI
snippet.description:
Setiap ketukan di HP, transaksi online, dan unggahan media sosial menghasilkan data. Bagaimana data sebanyak itu bisa diubah menjadi keputusan? Dan bagaimana AI bisa memahami teks, gambar, suara, dan video sekaligus?

Video ini adalah materi Sesi 13 mata kuliah Introduction to Information Technology (INF124104), Program Studi S1 Informatika, Fakultas Ilmu Komputer, UPN “Veteran” Jakarta, Semester Ganjil 2026/2027. Materinya disajikan dengan animasi dan contoh sehari-hari seperti kantin kampus, supaya konsepnya mudah dibayangkan.

Setelah menonton, kamu diharapkan mampu:
✅ Menjelaskan karakteristik big data: volume, velocity, dan variety (3 V)
✅ Memilih alat analisis data sederhana (spreadsheet, dashboard, SQL, Python) untuk mendukung keputusan
✅ Mengaitkan dimensi variety pada big data dengan Multimodal AI

Daftar isi:
00:00 Pembukaan
00:57 Peta topik Sesi 13
02:04 Sub-CPMK & indikator capaian
03:26 Apa itu big data? (sumber data & mengapa sekarang)

snippet.title: ggplot2 Full Course: Data Visualisation & EDA in R | R 104
snippet.description:
Charts are how analysis gets noticed. Learn ggplot2 properly, from the grammar of graphics to publication-ready plots, then use it to explore real data and find the story.

Every line of code is typed and run live in RStudio, so you see real output, real errors and how to fix them. Pause at the 'Pause and try it' exercises and code along.

What you'll learn:
- Why we visualise: Anscombe's quartet and the grammar of graphics
- Scatter plots, trend lines, histograms, density plots, boxplots and violins
- Bar charts done right: geom_bar vs geom_col
- Line charts, facets and small multiples
- Labels, themes, scales, colours and annotations that guide the eye
- Saving plots with ggsave
- A full exploratory data analysis workflow on three real datasets, ending in clear findings

This is video 4 of 6 in the free series R Programming Full Course: Beginner to Expert, which takes you from absolute beginner to expert in over 7 hours of hands-on R.
New here? Start with R 101 in the playlist: R Programming Full Course: Beginner to Expert.

NEXT: Statistics in R: Hypothesis Tests, Regression & Modelling (Full Course) (R 105), goes live 11 Nov.

snippet.title: Python Pandas Tutorial: Master DataFrames for Data Analysis from Scratch | HINDI#pandas#RAMARCURY
snippet.description:
Ready to master data analysis in Python? In this comprehensive tutorial, we dive deep into Pandas, the most popular data manipulation library in Python. Whether you're a complete beginner to data science or looking to sharpen your skills, this video will teach you everything you need to know about working with DataFrames.

By the end of this video, you'll know how to load, clean, filter, group, and analyze real-world datasets efficiently like a pro!

📚 What You'll Learn in This Video:
What is Pandas and why it's the core library for Python data science

Understanding Series vs. DataFrames

How to load data from CSV, Excel, and JSON files

Essential data inspection methods (head(), info(), describe())

Filtering, sorting, and selecting specific rows and columns

Handling missing values and duplicate data

Grouping, aggregating, and merging datasets (groupby, merge, concat)

A practical hands-on mini data analysis project

snippet.title: SQLvsPythonvsPySpark 20 Data Operations Cheat Sheet |Data Analytics & Engineering #Shorts #bigtable
snippet.description:
💻 SQL vs Python vs PySpark – 3 Tools, One Data Workflow!

Do you know how the same data operation can be performed using SQL, Python (Pandas), and PySpark?

This cheat sheet covers 20 common data operations with equivalent code examples across all three technologies.

📌 What you'll learn:

1. Read Data
2. View First & Last Rows
3. Select Columns
4. Filter Rows
5. Multiple Conditions
6. OR Conditions
7. Sort Data
8. Remove Duplicates
9. Count Rows & Unique Values
10. Group By & Aggregations
11. Inner, Left, Right & Full Joins
12. Union Operations
13. Add & Rename Columns

🚀 Why learn these tools?

- SQL: Query and manage databases.
- Python (Pandas): Analyse and manipulate datasets.
- PySpark: Process large-scale data efficiently.

🎯 Useful for aspiring Data Analysts, Data Engineers and Big Data Developers.

snippet.title: Data Science for Beginners! Real-Life Example + Basic Python Practical
snippet.description:
In this video, we explore "What is Data Science?" in a simple and beginner-friendly way.

We start with a real-life example of a school trying to understand why some students perform better than others. Through this example, we'll understand how raw data is collected, cleaned, analysed, and transformed into meaningful insights.

We'll also explore the different fields that come together in Data Science and understand its basic workflow/pipeline.

Finally, we'll move to a practical demonstration using Python, Pandas, and Matplotlib, where we'll analyse student data, calculate average marks, and create a visualisation (scatterplot) to understand the relationship between study hours and examination marks.


- What you'll learn:

What is Data Science?

How Data Science works in real life

The role of Mathematics, Statistics, Programming, and Domain Knowledge

The 5 major steps in a Data Science workflow

Basic data analysis using Python

Working with Pandas and Matplotlib

Creating your first data visualisation

This video is for anyone curious about Data Science, especially beginners who want to understand the fundamentals before diving into Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence.

Hope you learn something new!

And since this video is going live on Diwali, a very Happy and auspicious Diwali to everyone! 😄🪔

snippet.title: Tesla Optimus Gen 3 New AI Explained: Does a Smarter Robot End the Housekeeper?
snippet.description:
Tesla Optimus Gen 3 just got a new AI brain, and the big question is whether it ends the housekeeper. Here is what actually changed, what is still unproven, and why the mind is only half the fight.

Spotlight Moments:

- Decodes the shift from a scripted “player piano” robot to one you can talk to in plain words

- Compares the vending machine and the short-order cook to see why the brain matters more than the muscle

- Traces Optimus’s three-part pitch: car-style camera AI, learning by watching, and generalizing to new tasks

- Exposes the demo gap, where a human may be running the robot from a step away

- Weighs the real walls: unreliable hands, 10,000 tiny physical tasks, and trust across a thousand ordinary days

- Faces the privacy trade-off of a robot that has to study your rooms and routines to improve

If this breakdown gave you something to think about, like the video, subscribe, and turn on notifications so you catch every honest test of home robots. Share it with someone who is waiting on a robot butler.

Now tell me in the comments: did Tesla just clear the last real obstacle with the mind, or is the true wall doing the job flawlessly in a real home a thousand days in a row? And what one thing would change your mind?

snippet.title: What Are AI Agents? Agentic Systems Explained | Stanford CS329Z Lecture 1 with Diyi Yang
snippet.description:
Browse Stanford's online courses in Agentic AI: https://stanford.io/4AIRb2z

Lecture Overview:
What is an AI agent, and how is it different from an LLM workflow? In the first lecture of Stanford CS329Z: Engineering AI Agents (Fall 2026), Stanford professor Diyi Yang traces the history of agents from the 1973 actor model to ReAct and AutoGPT, breaks down the anatomy of a modern LLM agent (LLM core, planning and reasoning, memory, tools, and environment), and explains why the most powerful agent may not be the most reliable one. She also covers course logistics and the key challenges for agents: reliability, training, safety, and evaluation.

Speaker: Diyi Yang

Diyi Yang is an assistant professor in the Computer Science Department at Stanford University, also affiliated with the Stanford NLP Group, Stanford HCI Group and Stanford Human Centered AI Institute. Her research focuses on human-centered LLMs and human-AI interaction.  She is a recipient of IEEE “AI 10 to Watch” (2020), Microsoft Research Faculty Fellowship (2021), NSF CAREER Award (2022), and a Sloan Research Fellowship (2024).

Chapters:
0:00 Welcome & instructor introductions
1:18 Course overview & logistics
7:40 A short history of AI agents
14:00 ReAct, BabyAGI & AutoGPT: the agent boom
19:06 Q&A: Will model capabilities saturate?
22:05 Anatomy of an LLM agent
28:19 Planning & reasoning: CoT, ReAct, Reflexion
36:52 Q&A: ReAct vs. chain of thought
40:39 Multi-agent debate & orchestration
43:12 Agent memory: episodic, semantic, procedural
46:30 Tool use: Toolformer & Gorilla
53:31 Compound AI systems: workflows vs. agents
58:41 Tool calls & Model Context Protocol (MCP)
1:01:05 Key challenges: reliability, safety & privacy

Course website: https://cs329z.stanford.edu/

Watch the full CS329Z playlist: https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLPRcF5HR02_U&si=3Z4OYphngcmQ0GIy

snippet.title: Does AI understand what it says? Explained in 60 seconds
snippet.description:
Does AI understand what it says, or is it just a very fancy parrot? Round 1: philosopher John Searle's "Chinese room" (1980) — a man follows a rule book to answer notes in Chinese: perfect replies, zero understanding. Round 2: Othello-GPT (2023) — a small GPT trained only on lists of game moves, with no rules and no board, turned out to hold a map of the board inside, and editing that map changed its moves. Round 3: critics call language models "stochastic parrots" that stitch words together without meaning; others reply that predicting well requires a model of the world. Verdict: a draw — AI builds inner maps of the world, but whether that counts as understanding depends on what you mean by the word.

Sources: John Searle, "Minds, Brains, and Programs" (1980); Kenneth Li et al., "Emergent World Representations" (ICLR 2023); Emily Bender, Timnit Gebru et al., "On the Dangers of Stochastic Parrots" (2021).
AI vs Human, round 3 · AI in 60 seconds, part 17. More: youtube.com/@explainium.ai
#AI #ArtificialIntelligence #ChatGPT #TechExplained #Philosophy

snippet.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Under Investigation China Spy Allegations Explained
snippet.description:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is at the center of a developing investigation following reports about an alleged relationship with a businesswoman suspected by U.S. intelligence officials of having ties to Chinese intelligence.

Nvidia’s board has opened an independent investigation into whether Huang was targeted as part of a foreign-intelligence effort. The company says it has no reason to believe that Nvidia secrets or U.S. national-security information were compromised, but the review will examine all available information.

Huang has acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife, apologized to his family and colleagues, and said he will fully cooperate with the investigation.

This is an ongoing investigation—not a proven espionage case. The allegations remain allegations, and no public finding has established that sensitive information was shared or compromised.
